text:
anya: Hey team, noticed a production perf regression on Qwen-7B canary today. Tail token latency up ~25% on requests that hit Triton + FlashAttention when head_dim=96 (non-8/16 aligned). Fallbacks to SDPA are kicking in frequently.
chris: Ugh, that aligns with the 'non-aligned head dim' heuristics we've been trying to stabilize. Any profiling traces?
devon: Pushed a short perf snapshot from the canary, attaching nvprof-like summary below. Most time is in kernel selection + memcpy after KV merge.
maria: paste: ```
planner: choose_kernel(flash, head_dim=96) -> failed_compat_mask: true -> fallback=sdpa
triton: launch(batch=12, seq=512) -> kernel_time=13.2ms memcpy=5.4ms
continuous_batcher: observed varying past_lengths -> extra realign memcpy
```
anya: Two hypotheses: 1) FlashAttention mask handling for non-16 head dims has a path that triggers expensive masking loops, 2) our KV cache merging when batches have mixed past lengths is causing an extra copy that defeats the kernel's fast path.
chris: I saw a similar issue for Mixtral where RoPE scaling is applied and we end up padding heads to 128 in the runtime planner which fixed it but added token cost. Can we reproduce locally?
devon: Repro steps I used: ```
# quick repro
python perf_probe.py --model qwen-7b --dtype fp16 --head-dim 96 --batch 12 --seq 512 --use-triton true
# watch planner logs: RUNTIME_KERNEL_DECISION=verbose
```
maria: Quick note: when head_dim % 8 != 0 we currently prefer fallback SDPA only after a failed compile; that detection happens late. Move the compatibility check earlier in planner to avoid trying to compile FlashAttention at all. That reduces wasted compile/teardown time. :+1:
anya: Also saw a KV cache invalidation pattern: when a request in a batch has past_len=0 and others have >0, we pad keys then run memcpy to align shapes. That triggers a slower code path in FlashAttn implementation.
chris: Could we instead do per-request micro-batching by past_len buckets before kernel launch? That reduces memcpy but increases scheduling complexity. Tradeoffs?
devon: I benchmarked: grouping by past_len reduces total memcpy by ~60% and dropped kernel_time by ~18% for our canary traffic. But increases scheduler overhead ~1ms. Worth it for tail SLOs.
maria: Another mitigation: head-dim padding. We can pad head_dim to 128 when loading model on Dedicated, and record that mapping in model metadata so cost reports reflect padded compute. That avoids runtime branching but increases FLOPs.
anya: For private deployments we should make padding optional and expose a runtime flag: runtime.force_head_padding = [none|load-time|runtime-pad].
chris: Also, FlashAttention has a masking bug reported historically when RoPE scaling != 1.0 combined with non-power-of-two head dims. We should run unit tests for RoPE-scaling variants (0.95/1.0/1.07) across head_dim in {64,80,96,112,128}.
devon: I'll add CI jobs. Quick synthetic results: when head_dim=96 and rope_scale=1.07 FlashAttention path latency spikes 2x, SDPA stable.
infra-bot: Canary deploy #r-2026 completed: rolled back canary at 2026-03-18T15:04:22Z due to latency threshold breach.
maria: Proposed short-term changes: 1) Move head-dim compat check earlier, 2) bucket-by-past_len batching in continuous batcher, 3) opt-in head padding at load-time. Long-term: collaborate with FlashAttention upstream to fix mask loop and address RoPE-scale edgecases.
anya: Plan sounds good. Devon, can you open a PR for bucketed batching + planner check? Chris, can you run the RoPE scaling unit matrix overnight and dump artifact? I'll own the padding toggle and doc changes.
chris: On it. Will post perf matrix tomorrow morning. :coffee:
devon: Starting PR draft now. tagging @maria for review.
deploy-bot: Created canary rollback ticket: INF-5231.
anya: Thanks all — let's aim to have the planner check in a hotfix branch today, then follow with batcher change in the next sprint.
chris: FYI, I also raised this with the model-onboarding doc: mention head-dim compat notes for Qwen/Mistral/Mixtral.
maria: Noted. I'll update the Optimize docs and add an alert in Console that surfaces when head-dim causes fallback to SDPA.
anya: End of thread for now. I'll gather the artifacts and link in the PR.
